AITA for going through my brothers phone to try and find out what is wrong with him My brother (16) has not gone to school for two weeks and has missed 8 days in the 3 last weeks of the term before this term. I have recently learned that his grades are not as good as I thought, his highest grade is one 4, lowest is a U, and everything in between. (We are in the UK. 4 = C, U i think means ungraded/not attempted.)

My mum and I have tried every way we could possibly think of to help him, or to understand why he is struggling with going to school and why his grades are so low. He gives us nothing back, his answers to every question is “I dont know” or some other sarcastic remark. My mum is extremely soft with him because in the past, maybe 2 years ago he was depressed. Not clinically diagnosed, but he was hurting himself for a brief period of time. He didn’t respond to therapy. Then he all of a sudden he was as happy as can be, friends over all the time, confidence overflowing. Since then he gets away with EVERYTHING, with maybe a “stern” talking to, if anything, because my mum doesn’t want to be the reason he goes back to where he was. She was NEVER that soft with me (22F) but thats another topic for another day.

So since we tried talking to him, we tried asking him if there was ANY possible way we could help, we tried going to the doctors, we tried seeking help from his school teachers, we came  up with a week-by-week revision schedule with all three of us working together to improve his grades - he isn’t interested. nothing is helping the situation. 

I know that if my brother misses any more school, my mum will be fined or even sent to prison for failing to get him to school. He knows this too.

So AITA for snatching my brothers phone whilst he was on it and locking myself in my bedroom in order to try and get some information - maybe from his friends or his pictures or SOMETHING - to try and figure out what is bothering him so much that he’s too depressed to go to school? His reaction was obviously very negative. Our relationship may never be the same again. But i felt like i had no other choice. My mum and I wanted to help - we NEEDED to help, i felt like i had no choice but to do the thing that could very well break our relationship

but how am i meant to just let my brother fight his demons by himself. and what if he loses

TLDR: i took my 16yo brothers phone to try and find out what is making him depressed in attempt to help him as a last resort

AITA for telling my roommates their friend/boyfriend can't come over everyday? I'm currently in college living in a dorm, I have 2 other roommates for a total of 3 of us living in a tiny single room. I'm not the most sociable person, so I usually just leave the dorm all day when my roommates have friends over.

I HAVE tried to socialize with them and spend time with them, they are my roommates after all. I find that they talk for ages, but when I speak up, they look at me awkwardly and either say nothing or hesitantly laugh. I don't say things out of turn and I stick to the topic (example: they were talking about Marvel after seeing a commercial for a new show Chris Evans will be in. I chimed in saying 'Oh that's so weird to see him as anything other than Captain America!'...and they just kinda awkwardly looked at me without a word.) 

Since the beginning of the semester, Roommate A has had her boyfriend (Cam) over nearly every single day, up until visitation hours are over (12 am on weekdays, 2 am on weekends). Cam is very good friends with Roommate B, and if he doesn't come to the dorm with his girlfriend, Roommate B brings him along instead. He even has his own pillow and blanket here and he takes naps on the couch. 

Yesterday, I was in the dorm after working and was getting annoyed as I hear the 3 of them complain about a professor for 30-40 minutes. Right after they finish, I said I needed to talk to them all for a second.

Silence, no reply from any of them until I ask if its ok. A quiet "sure" from Roommate A,  so I continue (in a monotone voice) and say that Cam can no longer be here everyday, it bothers me, he is not my roommate. Please have him only come over on Thurs/Fri/Sat/Sun.

Silence again except now Cam just gets up and packs up without a word. I say he can stay since it's already 10pm. He replied in a shaky voice, which surprised me. I think he was mad. He mentioned something about having things to do anyways. Still silence and I had to urge a reply from the others.

Roommate A eventually says "sure we can figure something out." Roommate B says nothing still until I address her by name and she snaps back a reply "he's just my friend I don't really have any say if he's in the room or not."  She has complained to me about him being there too often and she's tired of it and yet she brings him here.

They all left immediately after that with no more words to me and I just felt so bad and guilty to drive all of them away like that. AITA?

So I told her that and she goes on to say that misgendering someone is the same as being racial to someone, which I think isn’t true. She then calls me a female (I’m a guy) since she feels I didn’t respect the transgender females gender, which is hypocritical as she literally told me that you don’t get to pick and choose what to call someone under any circumstance. I just believe to let live, if someone wants to call themself something, you should respect it but if you choose not to, it’s rude and shouldn’t happen; but it shouldn’t be the same as calling someone of color a racial slur. question:
AITA for not being there for my friend? Edit: people keep saying I should not have gone to the party if I knew I had the bridal fair the next day. I wasn't sure if I would be able to go the next day, and Becky and I decided together to go to the party that night before. Like texting back and forth to make sure the other was going so that we could share an uber back together because we knew we would be drinking. At the party, Becky again asked me to go and I agreed while drunk on the toilet. I had only said maybe before, if my work called me off that night. I usually sleep during the day because I have to be up from 7pm-7am for my job. I cant just sleep the night before and stay up all day and then remain up all night. I have to get sleep beforehand. 

So, my best friend is getting married in 10 months. Let's call her Becky. I'm her maid of honor. Its exciting and I'm really happy for her. I've never been a maid of honor before though. I'm struggling with this situation so far:

So Becky has already picked out her dress and decided on bridesmaid dresses. We spent an entire day shopping in a city an hour away and deciding on these things. 

Since then, she has invited the other bridesmaids and I to go to 2 events with her. The first was a florist visit last month so she could decide on the kind of flowers she wanted for the wedding. I originally said yes I would go, but then she had to change the date of the appointment to a day where I had to work. So I didnt go. 

The second event was yesterday. 3 days prior she had told me and other bridesmaids about this bridal fair she wanted to go to, and asked if we could go. I told her I would have to see how things went because I worked that evening. The event would basically take most of my sleeping time. But whatever. 

Saturday night comes along and Becky and I both get invited out to a birthday party of a mutual friend that night. We both had off, and we would see some good friends which included the other bridesmaids, so we all went. Everyone got wasted, most people not making it home before vomiting. I had a good time, things felt good. At the party, Becky asked me again if I would go to the bridal fair the next morning. She begged, saying only a couple of other older family members were going with her. Drunk me felt like Superwoman, so I said sure. Everyone got drunk af and went home. 

I went home at 2am, woke up at 5am with a splitting headache and a shit ton of stomach pain. I took ibuprofen and tried to get comfortable enough to sleep. No go. I chugged water. Still felt like shit. Now its 8am and I am extremely nauseous. I hadn't drank alcohol since 1am, I thought I had escaped nausea. My boyfriend was really worried I had something else going on because of the amount of pain I was in, and wanted me to go to the hospital, but I'm in the medical field so I felt like I knew when I would need to go to the doctor. I couldnt sleep still. It was 9:30am. The bridal fair was supposed to be at 11. I texted Becky to tell her I wasnt going to be able to go. I felt like complete crap. I apologized. 

I finally vomited, passed gas, and the stomach pains/nausea started to fade. It was 11:30. Becky had opened my message but not responded. I finally was able to fall asleep. At 1pm I woke up to a message from Becky, saying she was extremely disappointed in the fact that I wasnt there for her with the wedding planning. She said I never went to events with her and she would just have to learn to "lean on" someone else instead of me. 

I'm like...what? I spent a day with her picking out dresses. I am actively planning an expensive bachelorette party because she wants a destination one. I feel like I'm doing what I'm supposed to do. It has just been shitty timing for the other stuff. I told Becky this, she said it doesnt change the fact that I've let her down and been a disappointment to her. She then went on to say she doesnt accept my reasons for not going to the bridal fair (extreme nausea and pain). She said every other bridesmaid had messaged her the same thing and she expected more. 

I just... I don't know. In my family, you did not have the maid of honor or bridesmaids do shit like this. They help with bachelorette parties and stuff like that. It's just weird to me that Becky seems to expect this much of me and the other bridesmaids. Is this normal though? Am I being an asshole? 

Tl;dr bride is mad that maid of honor and bridesmaids cant make it to florist meeting and bridal fair. AITA for not being there?

AITA for insisting on giving someone, who I thought was my friend, a gift? This situation happened roughly 7 months ago, but I recently discovered this subreddit, and I thought it would be interesting to go back and reassess if anybody is the asshole here. This is also a throwaway account because I’m paranoid. 

I was friends with this girl who I met in 2016. She was the lead actress in a high school musical I was stage managing. Long story short, by the end of the show’s run I told myself I was in love with her. I boldly asked her to go out with me, and I was denied. I was bummed, but I was still happy I mustered up the courage to ask her. I hadn’t done something like that in a while.

Fast forward to 2017, and we still kept in touch after the show ended. I remember hanging out with her and other mutual friends at a 4th of July celebration. This made me really happy because it was the first 4th of July I spent with friends instead of with my family. Saw her in 2 other musicals she was in in spring 2018, met up with her during prom weekend, and she even invited me to her 18th birthday in July. 

After that, our friendship just fell apart so suddenly. I tried to meet with her before she moved to college, but my plans fell through. Then, this exchange of messages happened in December (see the Imgur album here - https://imgur.com/gallery/M80ZaOL). I took these screenshots in a different time zone (originally EST) so everything is off by 6 hours.

Between when she leaves me on read and my next text, I consult 3 of my closest friends for opinions on my situation. All 3 know her, but not enough to call them their friend. The consensus was that they all found it strange how even though we were good friends, she still refused to see me and accept my gift (a sweater and a formal dress. She had no idea what the presents were beforehand.) 1 of them suggested that my friendship with this girl was affected by her choice to “start fresh” in college, letting go of past friends in favor of making new ones, which I understood could happen, and it’s nothing personal. With this in mind, I texted her what can be seen in screenshots 4-7.

Huge blow to my self-esteem, and I thought I was over it, but here we are. 

Some questions I had at the time (and I suppose still have):
- Was it rude for her not to accept my gifts considering what they stood for? She wasn’t the only one I bought gifts for, and the others were happy I thought about them during the holiday season. Mind you, this is also the first time I’ve actually bought gifts for people who weren’t in my family.
- Was it too much of me to bring up the “shadow blocking” incident? In the moment, I brought it up because I wanted to call her out on her shady behavior. Should I have kept that information to myself?

I’ll try to respond to everyone’s judgments when I wake up in the morning. Hopefully I can close the book on this one once and for all.

question:
AITA for telling my nephew Santa isn't real in a game of 20 Questions? Well, the title basically sums it up, but I might as well tell the full story.

My BIL was doing a get-together for his birthday. Eventually, though, everybody started getting drunk, so I was about to leave, before my nephew spotted me and begged me to stay. So, I went in his room where he and my sister were waiting for BIL's friends to all go home. He suggested that we play 20 Questions, that game where someone thinks of a character for you and you have to figure out who it is my asking 20 or less yes-or-no questions. He wanted to go first, so my sister wrote *Santa Claus* on a piece of paper and taped it to his forehead.

The way we played it was that he would ask the questions while my sister and I would take turns answering them. Eventually it got to the question that was obviously going to come up and I was lucky enough to be the one forced to answer it.

"Is he a real person?"

Truth be told, I was actually thinking about how I should answer this from the moment we started the game, since I knew it was almost certainly going to come up. My sister hasn't spent Christmas with us since she got married, so I had no idea if her son knew Santa isn't real yet or not. I remembered how our dad told us the truth about Santa when I was 5/6 and my sister was 6/7 (which I do realise is quite early). I also thought back to how our daughter figured the truth out by herself when she was 7. Ultimately, though, my though process was this: surely my sister wouldn't choose Santa for this game if she expected to read her mind and go along with pretending that he's real. So, without hesitation, I blurted out, "No." Perhaps if I waited a bit before answering, my sister would have coughed or something to let me know that she wants me to lie, but alas, the milk was spilled and all I got from her was a disapproving glance.

My nephew soon ran out of questions and his final guess was Mario (he was able to figure out that it's a fictional character who's fat, has facial hair and dresses in a bright colour). Once he realised that it was actually Santa, he immediately pointed out that I said the character wasn't real. My sister tried to tell him that I said it by accident and I tried to go along with it, but eventually her son started crying. She seemed quite pissed and told me that "I should go".

On my drive home I started to feel increasingly guilty and today I woke up (quite late) to a bunch of messages from both my sister and BIL calling me an asshole who ruined Christmas for their son. Admittedly, I have no idea what age kids normally find about Santa out at, but 9 still feels like pretty old to still believe and get *that* upset upon finding out the truth. Apparently, though, he made quite a scene about it, both last night and this morning. I, of course, apologised, but BIL still said that I'm not getting invited to any more get-togethers. I'm sure this won't last and we'll all make up soon, but I would like to know if I really am the asshole in this situation or not.

My friend and I were talking about going to see Frozen last week.  Neither of us have kids, but we enjoy Disney movies and had been to see the last one together so thought we’d go together again. She said she’d look into times and let me know.   

Now I need to mention that my friend and I don’t live close to each other. I live in a big city and she moved out a few years ago, so we take it in turns to do things in each of our neighbourhoods. She drives to me, I take a train to her. Both journeys are about 40 mins each way.

I just really wished she’d asked me first, as we go to the movies together a lot and would never sit there.

- spending money on a train ticket and travelling all that way

to then have to ALSO sit and get a sore neck from staring up at the screen. I feel like I could have coped with everything else if we had decent seats. 

So I’m thinking of feeling ‘under the weather’ on the day and just do my own thing. She’s got her other friend to go with so it’s not like I’m abandoning her. And she won’t be out of pocket for the money spent. 

WIBTA for pulling out?

question:
AITA for hosting my daughter’s sweet 16 MY way?  My only child was born around the time of May that Memorial day falls. So, it’s become a tradition for me to host a large family gathering around that time, since the guests are off work. It’s nominally a birthday party. Some guests bring presents sometimes, sometimes not, and we have cake (*we* do, anyway, if my daughter does not eat it, that is her choice). But you could also call this party my yearly family reunion.

The problem is, ever since she was 11 years old, my daughter has been influenced into thinking she’s a vegan. As much as I persuade or sneak things past her, she hasn’t willingly used hide nor hair (ha!) of an animal for almost five years. Not even wool, which is really inconvenient for my shopping considering the fact that she grows like a weed.

Every year, she asks me to change the menu of her/my party to be meat free, milk free, and even egg free. In dramatic teenager fashion, “*I don’t want animals to be killed for my birthday*.” I tell her that she can’t control how other people eat. I’m obviously not going to look cheap to my family by serving them rice and beans. Nor will I be making alternative slop just so “she has something to eat.” There is plenty to eat, and it is gorgeous, she just chooses not to. Last year, she even did make a second cake out of pumpkin or some such. It looked ridiculous and went in the trash as soon as she’d cut a slice to eat with he rest of us. I am an excellent cook, and I like the table to look a certain way, especially when my *darling* sisters-in-law are here to nitpick.

This year, after the usual request to change the menu, my daughter “told” me that she won’t be attending her own birthday party. Instead, she’s going to meet friends at another girl’s house, where they will eat leaves and talk about her “mean mother” I’m sure. Ha! I told her she’s being ridiculous, that she’s not a real vegan anyway since I’ve been cooking the family’s rice in chicken broth for the past five years. (Rice is often the only thing on the dinner table she will eat, since she can’t see the meat.) In typical fashion, she cried and stopped responding.

So now I have a dilemma. I can’t exactly force her to stay and act convincingly happy, although she does know there will be consequences if she doesn’t.

I can let her win this little power struggle and change the menu of the party. This will teach her that If she kicks her heels long enough, she can force other people to bend around her weird demands.

Or I can host the party my way, and have my family awkwardly asking “Where’s the birthday girl?”

I could re-brand the party as a family reunion, but there will be questions, and family has already asked me this year about “her birthday party.”

I can't decide which option makes me look like more of a chump.

question:
AITA For cutting off friendship after 1 drunk night ? This happened a few days ago. TL;DR at the bottom

So I (24m)  was invited to my friends (28m) house for his birthday, I asked him if I could invite a friend (23f) and he said yes it's fine.

Arrive at the party we start having drinks, my friend shows up and we start playing drinking games. She and I have played drinking games before. All went well except she got drunk very quickly. I could see around the table people were getting slightly irritated by her who is now drunk to which I pulled her to the side and told her, I think it's best if she go gets some fresh air outside with the other people. 

Maybe after 10 mins we finished the game and went outside, 5 mins my friend starts throwing up, so I let her finish and guide her to the bathroom so she can finish throw up there and got her a spare wash cloth so she can wipe where needed because she spilled on her dress. While helping her, I ask if she wanted to lay down in the spare room and sleep for a bit to which she replied she doesn't feel comfortable sleeping in a stranger's house (fair enough). She wanted to go sit in her car, in the drivers seat to which I made it my duty to prevent that just in case she decides to drive off in that state.

After some arguing and she really went off on me to leave her the f*** alone and I'm not the boss of her etc. I suggested to her that I drive her home with her car and then take an uber back to the party but she said no. I told her she can sit in the passenger seat and to contact someone to fetch her then she said no her brother is on his way, a struggle ensued and I manage to get her car keys out of her hands as she was in no condition to drive.

Eventually she sits in the car while I have her car keys after she threatened to call the police 

After maybe 20-30mins the police arrives and we are in shock. We speak to the police and we let her talk first, (to my shock) she tells the police that I'm trying to sleep with her and that we drugged her (remember this friend and I know each other for 8 years by now). So I was shocked and we all denied her allegations. The police asked for the car keys and we gave it them, then we all just told her she must f*** off.

When I got home, I just sent her a text to tell her I've never been so humiliated in my life and that she should lose my number as I want nothing to do with her. Deleted her number and all social connections.

AITA for cutting off all connection with her and wanting to not be associated with her in anyway, effectively cutting her entirely out of my life ?

TL;DR Friend gets drunk, shouts at me in front of my friends, we take away her car keys, she calls the cops and when she leaves I message her to never contact me again.

question:
AITA for exploding on my father's wife Throwaway  

Hear me out on this one.

In regards to ages, I’m 17, Dad is 43, and father’s wife 27 or 28.

Six years ago, it came out during couple’s therapy that my father was cheating on my mom and that his mistress was pregnant. My mom initiated divorce. Six months after the divorce was finalized, my father married his now wife and they had three kids. My dad has apologized for his actions and we are still doing therapy, so one day I can truly forgive him.

I do not like my so-called stepmom, but in regards that she is father’s wife, I begrudgingly show respect. I have never called her out of her name until later in this story. If she speaks to me, I will say something back. If I am in her home, I will clean up after myself. However, I will always refer to her as my father’s wife and she will never be a prominent figure in my life. This is something she cannot accept.

I have never let my true feelings about her be known, until the other day. While at my father’ house, she attempted to make a cringe-worthy joke about my girlfriend with the saying “The blacker the berry the sweeter the juice,” and said that I was good enough looking boy and she was confused about why I would go out with a dark-skinned black girl and not someone white like myself. I guess the look on my face told her to shut up, so she changed the subject.

She then revealed that when my dad gets back from his TDY (Temporary Duty Assignment); she had booked a photoshoot for family portraits of us and she wanted to do a special photo of me and her two sons holding signs that say “Don’t mess with her,” with her 2-month-old daughter. I have never been in any of the previous family portraits because I refused to and my Dad said I didn’t have to.

I told her I was not going to participate

She asked why I was being difficult and that just she wanted family pictures with all of her children.

Six years’ worth of hurt came out. I told her she was a fool to ever think I was her child or that I considered her family. From my perspective, she was nothing, but my father’s racist side chick, who had nothing better to do, but chase after a married man and sit on her ass all day. I took it a step further and fully implied that her daughter wasn’t my father’s child because she looks nothing like him.

She turned red and started crying, saying how disrespectful I was and I had no right to talk to her in such a manner. I fully admit I called her a Bitch and stated she didn’t even deserve any respect from me because she didn’t respect my mother’s marriage and if she ever disrespected my girlfriend again, she would live to regret it. After realizing what I had said, I left and haven’t talked to her since.

Everyone that I have talked to say I should at least apologize for calling her a bitch and I don’t mind doing that.  However, certain people say I shouldn’t have gone off on her, because my dad was gone and she just had a baby, etc.

So who is the asshole?

AITA for not accomdating my roommate? OK so new throwaway acc,  I'll try to keep it simple 

-Me and roommate live together, not a college but we do go to college. There's  another roommate who isn't around much. Rent is spilt between all of us evenly

-My schedule is waking up at 6AM, shower, get dressed, make breakfast, pack my bag, finish any work from before etc. I leave by 7, I get to my college/or work at 8 

-Recently, roommate mentions that taking a shower so early is disturbing her because her room is next to the bathroom and the sound of water wakes her up and makes it hard to sleep after.  Sensitive sleeper

-I apologize and try to work it out. We both agree that 6:30 is better. Less time for me tho. 

-Next week roommate talks to me again and she doesn't appreciate me making breakfast so early. I ask why, she says the smell of food wakes her up and makes her hungry and since she's tired at such an early time it's not fair for her. It's also not fair not cooking for her and roommate #3. She asks if I can shower at 7 or something so the shower doesn't bother her. 

-I feel a little upset and tell her that she is being picky. I say 1. I have to be out the door by 7, and sometimes the trains are delayed. I can't risk being late 2.My schedule is already rushed 3. I don't have to cook for them since we all cook our own meals and I always clean after myself. 

-Roommate is upset and cuts off the conversation. 

-Next day I decide to go back to the schedule I was used to bc it gives me more time. I go shower. I step out the bathroom and roommate is there and yells at me that I am being petty for going back to waking up at 6. I tell her that I am used to waking up at this time and there's no need for me to accomodate her since she's picky. She says I'm a bitch, I say that her shower issue is her problem and to wear earplugs then. 

-Argument breaks out, I go off to work. When I come back, roommate #3 asks what happened because the other roommate told her what's up. I explain my side, roommate #3 says I am 100 percent selfish in this issue. 

-Roommate #3 explains that I am the wrong one because I went back to showering at 6 when Roommate said the sound of the shower ruined her sleep and maybe she has a lot of work between college and her job. I say I shouldn't be accommodating if she thinks I should be making breakfast for everyone and if it disturbs my schedule. I don't complain when she showers. Roommate #3 says that this is exactly why I'm the selfish one/in the wrong because I'm not thinking of how the other roommate feels and I don't have sleep sensitivity so I can't say "but I don't complain"

I went to bed and kinda thought it over. Idk. Reflecting on it, part of me feels bad for the possibility of waking her up by showering so early, but then I feel that it is ridiculous and there's no reason I should accomodate. Idk. Wanted to know what reddit thinks.

question:
AITA for thinking my girlfriend's wealthy parents should help her with her medical bills? So 2 years ago my girlfriend had surgery for an ovarian cyst and at that time she was diagnosed with endometriosis. Since then, she's had 4 ovarian cysts bursting this year alone with 2 of them resulting in ER visits and 1 resulting in an urgent care visit. She's been on birth control for more than a year and it's caused other issues (depression).

She is still on her parent's health insurance and the first ER visit was a hefty bill and she managed to set up a payment plan with the hospital that she is just about to finish paying off now. She is also currently on a payment plan for the urgent care visit.

Both of these bills along with other bills eat up her entire paycheck. All of these financial issues have had a major impact on her mental state and worsened her depression. It seems like most days if she's not dealing with chronic pain from her endo she's dealing with financial troubles and it's an endless cycle.

The second ER visit just happened a week ago and was a reluctant visit since she really could not afford to go. We ended up having no choice when she developed some more alarming symptoms. Before going, I suggested since she was so bogged down with medical bills already to call her mom and see if she could help her with this bill. In the past, I have offered several times to cover her medical bills because of the stress but my girlfriend is adamant that I do not help her since we aren't married. There is also tension with her mother and I because her mother does not want me to think that they cannot/will not take care of their daughter with medical bills.

So we went however her mom gave her a long speech about how this was irresponsible and that the only reason my girlfriend had these medical bills was because she needed to learn a lesson about not leaving medical issues to the last second. Flash forward to yesterday, there is a huge argument and her stepdad essentially states that my girlfriend is entitled for thinking they should help her with her medical bills. My girlfriend's argument is that she has never asked for their help before and has been paying for her own phone, car, insurance, etc. since she was 16. His argument is that the parent does not have a responsibility to help their adult child with medical bills regardless of the situation or the context.

Her parents make well over 6 figures, both have new cars, a half a million dollar home, and just came back from a very expensive Europe trip. My own parents have always taught me that family helps family and even though my parents aren't wealthy in the slightest, I knew that in my early 20s if I was struggling I could always rely on their help. I just can't wrap my mind around how her parents can flaunt their wealth so openly and yet stand by while their own daughter suffers from an unpreventable chronic illness/chronic pain while also juggling depression and financial woes that they could easily take away without putting them into any financial trouble whatsoever.

I’ll try to keep this short. Genuinely interested in hearing what y’all think.
I met my roommate about 4 months ago. We clicked instantly, she’s super cool and we live very similar lifestyles. We’ve had no problems thus far. 
Her 25th birthday is in January, so I started to think about what might be a fun surprise to do for her. She made it clear that she loves thoughtful gifts more than just gifts for the sake of it, so I thought it would be fun to surprise her with a trip to a neighboring state and a weekend that was all about her (in a place she had specifically mentioned wanting to go). I reached out to all her friends and started organizing. A couple days after I started organizing, I got wind of a separate birthday celebration that was happening for her, involving clubbing and a different location. 
So I spoke to her and told her that I had a surprise planned (didn’t tell her what the surprise was, just that I was trying to put something together for her) and asked her what she specifically wanted for her birthday. She asked me to not reveal the surprise and to ask her friends to figure out what she wants.
So I went back to her friends and tried to figure out another plan and was immediately shut down. So then I just tried to jump on board with the plan they had going, but it sounded like it was going to be really expensive for a few nights out in a city we don’t live in (airbnb, ubers, brunch, club cover fees, drinks, dinner and lunch out, etc). I specifically told her friend that I needed to think about it but that if I didn’t go I was going to find another way to make it up to my roommate. I had fully planned on speaking to her about it in person and asking her directly if she cared about me being there.
Well I found out today that her friend went behind my back, revealed the surprise, told her I wasn’t going anymore (I have the texts to prove that I never said that), and lied about why I wasn’t going anymore (she said that I didn’t want to/it didn’t interest me). My roommate then texted me very angry and I was dumbfounded. 
Here are some additional details that might be important:
1) One of my parents JUST died (less than a month ago). I’m in a deep depression that she doesn’t seem to give two shits about.

Am I the asshole for possibly (now, likely) not going to her birthday celebration?

question:
AITA for answering questions literally instead of telling the asker what they want to know? Okay, so I'm a fourth generation Korean American. I don't know a lick of any languages other than English and a bit of Spanish I learned in school. I've never been to Korea, nor do I want to go. My dad is the only person in my family who speaks any Korean or has been to Korea. And the only thing I know about Korean culture is what other people tell me. In short, I'm only Korean by blood and nothing else. I don't bring it up and I don't act any different from an average American, but I still always invariably get The Question from coworkers/strangers/Tinder peeps. Now, The Question comes in many different forms, but it's purpose is to elicit my ethnic background.

Here are some forms The Question takes and how I answer them. (These are actually what people say)

* "Where are you from?" Los Angeles
* "No, I mean, where were you born?" Los Angeles
* "No, like, where are you REALLY from?" ...Los Angeles
* "Where are your parents from then?" Well my mom was born in Los Angeles, but my dad is from Houston...
* "What's your nationality?" American
* "What kind of Asian/Chinese are you?" Asian American. No Chinese. (note: There are many people who are convinced that 'Asian' and 'Chinese' are interchangeable)
* (my personal favorite) "What are you?" Yeah, let me sum up my entire existence and identity with my race...

Having had this conversation at least once a week since I was a kid, I know exactly what the asker mean by the first question. I know I'm being cheeky, but this question always rubs me the wrong way. It's also kinda funny/sad to see people try to find different ways to ask this question so I let it run as long as they keep trying. And I only tell them the literal answer of the question they ask. Yesterday (after about three failed attempts at The Question) a coworker said that I was being rude since I knew what she was asking. My rationale for my behavior was that if they do want to know this information about me, they should be able to ask the right questions. It's not that hard. 'What's your ethnicity/ethnic background' is perfectly fine. I feel like all those other forms of The Question innately make the person being asked The Question seem more 'different' or 'foreign'. So, AITA for answering someone's questions literally instead of telling them what they want to know?

​



When I still lived in LA, there were a lot of people like me, Asian Americans whose parents and grandparents were born in the US. I didn't get The Question quite as much then. But after moving to the East coast for college and work, I get The Question all the time. I'm guessing it's because there's not as many Asian families that have been here for generations like in the West (best) coast. Let's go back to The Question. If a non-Asian in Virginia who grew up in LA was asked "Where are you from?" how would they respond? Would they say, "Oh my family has roots in Scotland and Ireland"? No, they would say they're from LA. So, why should I answer any differently? Why do **I** have to accommodate to other's expectations of me that are obviously double standards and assumptive?

I told her that I'm open to it, but I'm not going to be the first to reach out. I feel like I deserve an apology because he was indifferent to me growing up and I don't feel like I should have to be the one to begin to mend things over. She feels like I should make the first move.

Backstory:

Me and my Dad don't have much of a relationship. He was in and out of my life for the first four years and my grandmother raised me until I was 7 and we all moved in together. Even during that time, It was never quite positive. I was the eldest kid of three and my dad remarried.  Because of this, my two younger siblings often got preferential treatment growing up. They would often argue, fight with other kids and even steal and rarely were  grounded but I'd be treated like a menace if I did so much as not sweep the floor to their liking. I remember once, after Visiting my biological mom for a week or two, my dad ground me for a week for just about no reason. Every time I'd  try to confide in him, or ask for advice, He'd berate me at best or bring it up at some point later on to make fun of me if I annoyed him.

Even as I got older, he never really invested much time in me; I was great in choir and in just about every concert I'd have a solo. Despite this, he'd just drop me and my grandmother off and go home and watch TV.  It kinda hurt being praised by so many strangers but my own father couldn't care less. I even won a free trip to DC once because I won a Japanese language speaking contest and he was more interested in figuring out how my clothes got into his hamper.  Growing up it was always this. Any good thing I'd do he'd ignore but if I slipped up he'd have a field day and wouldn't let it go for weeks.  He called me a Failure at 15 for not having a job, and once I did, charged me rent. And the rent didn't go to anything responsible, like a college fund. I asked him and he laughed at me... It just went to my stepmom's pocket.

 The final straw that broke the camel's back was back when I was 23 and going through a rough patch. I won't go into detail but I was teetering on homelessness and barely eating. I asked him for $40 for food out of desperation, and he said he didn't have it. I found out days later that he flew out to Michigan first class and stayed at an expensive hotel for a vacation.

Despite this, I recently borrowed my stepmom(his wife) $750 to get her car out of repossession. Only reason I did that was because she was helping out my younger sister with rides to her work and she has a young child. I'm not sure if I'll ever actually get it back. It was the first time any one of them has called me in probably two or three years.

There's plenty of other stories but I feel like this gives a good overview of our relationship. So, AITA for feeling like I shouldn't have to be the one to reestablish communications?

Needless to say it was all very painful and even more so when family decided to make it about themselves.

Fast forward some more and we announce we were pregnant with our daughter. At first everyone was happy for us and offering to help with whatever. question:
AITA for lying and saying that I can't have kids? I am a 30yo woman, I have a boyfriend of 7 years and we are planning on marriage. Neither of us want kids. I am ok with kids! I just really don't want them. 

Monday night I was on a walk with a new-ish friend. She is a older than me by a little, in her early 40s. We were speaking of my recent recovery from a long term illness, and she was saying how it's good that I am healthier now because I'll be wanting to have kids with my SO soon - "maybe two!".

I replied "Hmm, nah, I wont be having children" trying to keep it casual and move the conversation on. But she pressed the issue. 

I can't remember verbatim how it went *exactly*, but she would keep arguing whenever I would say "No, I wont be having kids" after that. i.e saying "Oh you MIGHT do". I'd reply "No I wont be having kids!". She would press more, "but it might happen?". Again, I'd say no. She'd say "But you and (boyfriend) have been together quite a while now, you talk of marriage, you might be having them soon!" etc.

And honestly I got super annoyed. I couldn't believe that at 30, someone was arguing with me about this. I am an adult and know my own mind on this. I was also SLIGHTLY annoyed that she related the benefits of me getting better from a serious illness to me now being 'healthy to have kids' rather than, you know, it being a good thing that I am healthier for myself. Like somehow my purpose in life is to have babies. But that was probably be looking too much into it I guess... Anyway.

I didn't even think about it at all before I said it... but I was so annoyed I blurted out "I wont be having kids because I can't have them!"

She went quiet instantly and went "Huh?" and I panicked and said "Yeah I can't have kids, I have dodgy plumbing, nothing works in there" and she went "Oh right" and went completely quiet, before we changed the topic.

I was relieved that she wasn't going on about it anymore. However, since then, I have felt guilty for lying about something that's quite serious and very sad for a lot of women who can't have kids, but want them. At the same time, I really like how it got her off my back...

One of my (supportive) friends pointed out that I am getting to the age where I am likely to be prodded about it *more* nearing 40, rather than less like I thought I would be, and that thought is really exasperating... and even as guilty as I feel for lying to my friend about the integrity of my 'plumbing', I can't deny it worked a treat to get her off my damn back.

AITA for lying... ... and WIBTA if I lied like this again in the event others get on my case about it as relentlessly as this friend did?

AITA for taking my father's keys away and demanding more information My mom calls me at 7pm last night and says my 73 year old father went to a Drs appointment at 1pm and hasnt returned home or called. He was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis almost 20 years ago and it has slowly been breaking him down. He walks hunched over and uses a cane and also seems less lucid. 

I live 3 states away so I dont see him regularly but I have noticed the changes when I do visit. Hes mostly retired so he only leaves the house occasionally. Other than that he stays in his room. My parents have also been emotionally divorced for about 25 years, they are just roommates who share a last name now. They hate each other. Mom has no idea what his dr name is or where it is. Nothing.

Anyways so my sister and I start blowing up his phone. Goes straight to voicemail. She lives there so starts heading over to their house while I call the city hospitals. Hes not there. 

Finally at 745pm my dad calls my mother to say hes coming home and he'll explain when he gets there. An HOUR later he arrives and said he got lost going to the appointment. Apparently he drove around for 7 hours but during that time he did manage to call the dr to reschedule. He didn't think to call any of us for help or anything.

My sister and I feel like he shouldn't be driving by himself anymore and we need to get power of attorney while he is still competent to sign. Our mom said she will drive him but we have a feeling eventually she will get bored with being nice and send him off by himself just so she doesn't have to do it. He can be very grouchy and mean so I dont really blame her for not wanting to go head to head with him.

My sister has 2 kids and 2 jobs and I live far away with 2 kids so neither of us are in a position to be his driver/help right now. My husband says we are assholes for trying to control my dad and take away his freedom. He thinks my dad was just trying to get away from my mom for a while. I feel like 7 hours of being lost in the city you've lived in forever in excessive and dad might not be in his right mind enough to drive anymore. We plan on have a sit down with mom and dad tomorrow to discuss all this but my husband said my father will hate me for it and now I'm having second thoughts.

AITA For not letting my SIL see my son while she is in rehab for a month? This is a throwaway account.

**Background info:**

I (20F) have a son who is almost 1. My sister-in-law is about 24, and is currently in rehab for alcoholism. 

Before she went to rehab, she would disappear, for days at a time, binge-drinking. Then she would go to family events and church as if nothing was going on. The weekend before she went to rehab, the family had plans to get together for a kind of late Mother's Day lunch. Instead of showing up, my SIL went out the night before and got completely wasted and was really sick the day of the lunch. She's a petite woman, so she gets *really* sick. A few days later she agreed to go to rehab. 

At this rehab facility, she is not allowed contact for 7 days. After that, she can have phone calls whenever and visitors on Sundays for a short period. 

**The situation that makes me question whether IATA.**

The other day, my son and I went to lunch with my MIL and GMIL. During lunch, they both told me that I have to bring my son to visit my SIL in rehab, because we "need to show that we support her", and because she "misses *son's name* terribly". They said that my SIL has been telling the other girls at this facility about how cute *her baby* is, and I need to bring him so that she can show him off. They also told me not to worry, because the place is a huge mansion and super secure, and no one is even allowed to bring bags in. (I'm not sure why this is supposed to make me feel more comfortable with the situation? I cant bring a diaper bag into a place that we will be for about 3 hours, so that's inconvenient, but that's okay).

Anyway, I had a bad taste about the whole thing and just kept telling them that I would talk to my husband (their son/grandson). 

When I got home, I told my husband everything that was said, and I also expressed to him the following: 

I'm not comfortable bringing my son to a rehab facility, even if it is "safe". I also kind of feel like they are using my son as a "reward" for her being in rehab.. I dont know how to explain it, but that's how I feel. They said that she misses him, and that she wants to see him, but my thing is.. if she had not gone out binge drinking, she could have seen him. 

I'm proud of her for agreeing to go into rehab, but she has only been there for a little over a week or so. Why should I let her see my son? She can see him when she gets out. 

I also feel uncomfortable because they said that she wants to "show" "her baby" off. 

Anyway, my husband agreed with me and said that he will visit her alone. He told his family this and they think we are both assholes because we are "withholding" our son from my SIL and "giving the impression that we don't support her".

So, AITA? Or, I guess, AWTA?

Also, I am allergic to cats. And so is he. 
I take an allergy pill, but living surrounded by dander is quite different than visiting dander.

When my anxiety runs high, I do look for things to "fix" but this is not the case. I acknowledged his point but asserted that I was asking BECAUSE I CAN'T BREATHE. 

He went silent, which as good as killed the conversation.

Yesterday, one of his cats climbed onto my dresser and chewed up an item of mine with sentimental value. It's from Mexico and I'm in the US, so I can't exactly go to the store and buy another. 

I started crying and my boyfriend's solution was that I should "just put my stuff on a shelf so the cats can't get it". 

I don't think I should strip all of my furniture so the cats can continue climbing on it. I think someone who works in an animal Care field should probably spend a little more time training his cats not to walk on tables/dressers/etc. 

So, AITA for wanting a pet and allergy-free bedroom?

I did not file for child support because my ex insisted he would pay for anything the baby needed, and I felt bad for him being unemployed at the time. At first, he was just coming to see the baby whenever he felt like it, and I got fed up. Especially because any time I said, "I'm sorry, you can't take the baby right now, we have other plans," he would accuse me of trying to kidnap his son.

I insisted that, if he didn't want to go to court for custody, he had to agree to a parenting plan with me. No more showing up whenever he feels like. That was a battle itself, but eventually we agreed that he would have the baby each week from noon on Wednesday until 6:30 PM Thursday. Fine, Great. Done. Or so I thought.

He initially stuck to the schedule, but soon I was getting calls Wednesday morning, "Hey, can I just pick up baby after his nap?" Or, "Something came up, I'll be there at six." I gave him leeway because he works in construction (when he's working) and he was giving me a heads up.

The past couple of weeks, he has just shown up unannounced, today while I was getting my son ready for his nap, last week at some random time in the afternoon. I told him today that this behavior was not OK with me, and I needed him to communicate with me before picking up our son.

He said, "I have no way to communicate with you." The reason for this is that he blocked my number, which I am fine with, because out texting situation has been toxic, BUT he absolutely can reach me on my home phone, which he has done in the past. It was a ridiculous excuse, and then he blamed ME for his "inability" to contact me. I got upset with his lies and his manipulation and told him, "If you refuse to communicate with me about our son, expect to get served with a child support order."

Then I became the bad person who reneged on my "promise" not to make him pay child support. I was trying to manipulate him, he said, because he had left me for another woman. He says it is revenge, I say it is money that my child and I are owed, I was nice not to make him pay in the first place, and I have every right to except communication about our child (plus, if he we can't contact each other, what about an emergency?)

She struggles with complex PTSD in relation to her upbringing, as well as past relationships. Especially one where she was raped and had an abortion.

Last night I asked if she had heard of the controversy surrounding the song and how it had been pulled from the radio, just making small talk. I was expecting small talk and got an earful. I attempted (poorly) to relate why I personally thought the removal of the song was excessive and set a bad precident for artists past and present. I tend to look at a much broader picture and enjoy reading about the history of songs and looking into their meaning. I didn't do any of that before I stepped on that particular landmine.

I didn't want to trivialize her views, but I still wanted her to understand why I felt the way I did. Without any evidence beside my gut and a cursory read of an opinion piece over at the CBC.

Needless to say, I slept on the couch. 
I woke up to another shouting match, and having read into more of the history and circumstances around the writing and original (pre Neptune's Daughter) thought it would be a great idea to try again to offer my point of view, back with further knowledge on the subject. You know, instead of just backing down and waiting until shit blows over to apologize for being insensitive. 

I feel like I ruined our Friday night, possibly our whole weekend. As if I needed another reason to hate Christmas music.

They told me that they live up the road ( 4 miles) away, which i will refer to county B, the hotel is on the very outskirts of County A,  County B being 2 miles away.

when the taxi was 2 minutes away the guests asked why I ordered a taxi from county A when they said I knew they lived in County B? I apologised and said that they did not specify a taxi company and I told them I got a taxi from a taxi company that was closest to the hotel.

Basically, I was coming back through the town and this old fart pulls out of a parking lot on the other side of the road, comes all the way over to my side, making me swerve and crash into a telephone pole, totaling my car. Not only that, but when he swerved the opposite way, a person collided with him and their passenger suffered a broken arm.

When the State Troopers arrived (my college is in a small town), I flew off the handle at the old man. But man I was fuming all day and night into the next day. My parents brought me a rental (we had good renter's insurance) and I just broke down in my apartment just out of anger and hatred.

In the end, the troopers gave me a police report with a signed statement from a witness and just told me to call my insurance company when I could, which I did. I've since gotten a new car.

Looking back, I realize how little my anger served me and that there were bigger things at the stake than just my car. AITA for wanting to include my husband’s son in family photos and being hurt by his outburst?  

Six years ago, I married my husband after his divorce from his ex-wife. I know the start of our relationship wasn’t ideal, but we’ve been building our life together since, and we now have three children. My stepson, who is 17, has never really warmed up to me, but I’ve tried to remain respectful of his boundaries while still hoping we could form a closer bond. For example, he refuses to call me his stepmom, referring to me only as my husband’s wife, and he’s made it clear I’m not a big part of his life. I said it would mean a lot to me to have photos with all of the kids, including him, so we could look like a more cohesive family.

However, he refused, and when I pressed him, he snapped. He unleashed years of pent-up anger, calling me his dad’s “racist side chick,” accusing me of breaking up his parents’ marriage, and going so far as to imply that my youngest child isn’t my husband’s. He also called me a “bitch” and said I didn’t deserve any respect from him and that if I ever disrespected his girlfriend again, there would be consequences.

I was devastated and started crying. I feel I’ve tried hard to be patient and understanding toward him, and I didn’t expect such cruelty in return. Maybe I could have done better—my joke about his girlfriend was poorly thought out, and I know the situation I entered with his father years ago was not easy. But I’m just trying to build a family for my kids and, hopefully, include him in it.  

So, am I the asshole for trying to include my stepson in family moments and for being upset at how he went off on me?
